title: Number of Ways to Build Sturdy Brick Wall
summary: Given the height and width of a brick wall, along with an array of unique brick widths where each brick has a height of 1 and a width corresponding to an entry in the array, determine the number of ways to build the wall such that no two adjacent rows have bricks aligned at the same position, except at the ends of the wall.
statement: Given the height and width of a brick wall, along with an array of unique brick widths where each brick has a height of 1 and a width corresponding to an entry in the array, determine the number of ways to build the wall such that no two adjacent rows have bricks aligned at the same position, except at the ends of the wall. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Each row exactly fills width using unlimited bricks from the distinct positive widths list.
Adjacent rows may not share an internal vertical seam; the two outer wall edges do not count.
Return the number of height-row walls modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: A row matters to the next row only through its internal seam positions.
Enumerate every row seam mask, precompute pairs with no shared set bit, then use height-layer DP.
Start one way per row; for each higher layer sum prior ways from compatible masks and apply the modulus.
Every sturdy wall is a sequence of row masks with pairwise-adjacent compatibility, exactly the transitions counted by the DP.
editorial: Every sturdy wall is a sequence of row masks with pairwise-adjacent compatibility, exactly the transitions counted by the DP.

tests.explanation: The compatible row sequences [1,2] over [2,1] and the reverse give two sturdy walls.
A one-row wall may use [2] or [1,1], so return two.
